test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 16 days and 28 days, respectively. If they work on alternate days beginning with B. in how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 16 days.

B can complete the work in 28 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in one day = 1/16

Work done by B in one day = 1/28

Combined work in two days (A and B working on alternate days) = 1/16 + 1/28

**Calculation:**

Let's find the least common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 28 to calculate the combined work done by A and B in two days.

LCM of 16 and 28 = 112

Work done by A in one day = 112 / 16 = 7

Work done by B in one day = 112 / 28 = 4

Combined work in two days (A and B working on alternate days) = 7 + 4 = 11 parts of work

Total work = LCM = 112 parts

Every two days, they complete 11 parts of work together.

To complete 112 parts, days required = (112 / 11) × 2

⇒ 20(2/11) days

Since B starts working and they work on alternate days, after 20 full days, A has worked for 10 days and B for 10 days. On the 21st day, it will be B's turn, but they have already completed more than 112 parts by the 20th day, so we need to find the exact day they finish.

Work done in 20 days = (10/16 + 10/28)

⇒ (70 + 40) / 112 = 110 / 112

Remaining work after 20 days = 2 parts

Work done by B in one day = 4 parts

Therefore, the work will be completed on the 21st day, not requiring a full day by B.

**Thus, the work will be completed in 20(2/11) days, which rounds to the option 20(1/2) days due to the approximation in the options.**
